factProposals.value: Assets move through a lifecycle with only allowed status moves; retired is final.
Condition readings use a good/fair/poor/critical scale, are append-only, and the current condition is the latest by observed time.
A staff dashboard at /assets shows the inventory with filter, search and paging, plus lifecycle, condition and maintenance tasks with overdue flags.

Data entry errors name each wrong field; illegal or out-of-date status moves are refused and audited; condition discrepancies (critical but active, late older reading, retired with open work) are flagged for a person.

decisions.statement: Discrepancies are flagged and audited, and the status is left for a person to change.
decisions.rationale: the system should not decide an asset is out of service on its own

decisions.statement: A refused status move also discards the condition reading sent with it.
decisions.rationale: half-applied updates would leave the record inconsistent

limitations.statement: The status moves and the condition scale were chosen during the build and need confirming with the City's asset managers.
No load test for about 80 users and no recurring maintenance schedules.
Condition and maintenance are not sent to GIS.
